title: game/world.json
description: The procedural world's numbers (B01): the vertical range and sea level, the climate fields, the height model's splines and the snow and tree-line thresholds. Loaded by WorldGenData (Vocaterra.Game.Core); GameDataValidator checks the values (whole chunk layers, rising spline inputs, a river and lake bed below the sea, ordered ramps). Every number is a whole number: lengths in blocks, field values in thousandths of their range.

generated_by.description: Who or what wrote the file (hand-authored).

minY.description: The lowest block row; a multiple of 16.

maxY.description: One above the highest block row; a multiple of 16.

seaLevel.description: The water's surface; every column below it fills to it.

latticeBlocks.description: The spacing of the lattice the fields are sampled on and interpolated from.

lapsePer100Blocks.description: The fall of the temperature, in thousandths of its range, for every 100 blocks above the sea.

continents.description: The continentalness as continents (B02b redo): jittered cells, a share of them open sea, a channel of sea along every border; continentalness is the signed distance from the coast. Optional; without it the continentalness is plain noise.

cell.description: The cells' side in blocks; the continents are about this wide.

jitter.description: How far a cell's point strays from its centre, in thousandths of half the cell.

seaBlock.description: The side in cells of the blocks the cells are grouped in; each block holds a fixed number of sea cells, so the sea's share is the same everywhere.

seaPerBlock.description: The cells of each block, at random, that are open sea; fewer than the block's cells.

channel.description: The most sea each side of a border, in blocks (at most a quarter of the cell).

channelMin.description: The least sea each side of a border, in blocks; at least 1, so land cells are never joined and the sea is one ocean.

widthCell.description: The cell in blocks of the noise that varies the channel between its least and most.

coastCell.description: The cell in blocks of the noise that bends the coast (a warp of the plane).

coastBlocks.description: How far that warp moves a point, in blocks; at most a fifth of coastCell so it never folds.

scaleBlocks.description: The blocks that make 1000 thousandths of continentalness.

roughCell.description: The cell in blocks of the first octave of the noise added to the distance from the coast, so the coast wanders at every scale (B02b round 3). Optional (none).

roughBlocks.description: How far that noise moves the coast, in blocks (at most a quarter of the cell); the field keeps every channel at least half its least width each side, so land cells are still never joined.

salt.description: A number mixed into the cells' hash: another salt is another arrangement of the same kind of world. Optional (0).

base.description: The base height in blocks by continentalness.

rangeFactor.description: How much of the peaks shows, in thousandths (0 to 1000), by erosion.

peaks.description: The height the ridges add, in blocks, by ridges.

calmAmplitude.description: Hill height in blocks where the range factor is 0.

ruggedAmplitude.description: Hill height in blocks where the range factor is 1.

softCapAbove.description: Above this height the ground rises at half rate.

step.description: The shelf height in blocks; 0 or 1 for none.

width.description: How far from zero, in thousandths, the river field still carves.

depth.description: How deep the water stands in the middle of the river, in blocks: the bed is this far under the water's surface.

peakFadeFrom.description: The height in blocks that the ranges' peaks add to the ground, from which a river begins to fade out: a river does not cross a crest, it rises on each side in the foothills. Optional (none).

peakFadeTo.description: The height the peaks add where the river is gone; above peakFadeFrom.

valley.description: How the valley of a river climbs the high ground (B02b redo): above from the river's water stands deeper under the ground the higher the ground is, and the valley widens with the height.

from.description: The land height in blocks above which the valley widens and the floor rises.

widthPer10Blocks.description: The thousandths of the river field the valley widens by for every 10 blocks of ground above from.

depthGrowth.description: How much deeper the valley is, in thousandths of a block, for every block of ground above from.

water.description: The level of the water of the rivers and lakes (B02b round 3): the smooth ground of the column less the hills' amplitude, clearance blocks and the valley's depth, in steps of step blocks above the sea level and never under it, so a river's surface steps down its valley in flat reaches and a lake is flat at its own height. Optional (a step of 3 and a clearance of 2).

step.description: The height of a step of the water's surface, in blocks.

clearance.description: How many blocks under the smooth ground, besides the hills' amplitude, the surface stands.

depth.description: How deep the water stands in the middle of the lake, in blocks.

peakVariation.description: How the peaks' height varies along a range (B02b redo): scaled by a share from minShare to all over a smooth noise, so a spine rises to summits and falls to saddles. Optional.

cell.description: The noise's cell in blocks; the summits are about this far apart.

minShare.description: The thousandths of the peaks' height at a saddle.

coast.description: Near the sea the peaks fade out and the hills calm down (B02b), so the shore is a gentle shelf and no rugged island rises from the water. Optional; without it the peaks and hills are the same everywhere.

peaksFrom.description: The continentalness, in thousandths, below which the peaks show nothing.

peaksTo.description: The continentalness above which the peaks show in full; above peaksFrom.

hillsFrom.description: The continentalness at and below which the hills keep only hillsFloor of their amplitude.

hillsTo.description: The continentalness above which the hills keep all of it; above hillsFrom.

hillsFloor.description: The share of the hills' amplitude, in thousandths, that remains at the coast.

flatFrom.description: The ground height in blocks at and below which the hills are gone, so no speckle of flats and pools lies just over the sea. Optional (0: none).

flatTo.description: The ground height in blocks above which the hills are whole again; above flatFrom.

pass.description: The lock of the exit through the east ring (B08b): the pass opens when every required lesson is complete (or under the cheat setting) and stays open.

requiredLessons.description: The ids of the lessons that must all be complete; each must exist in game/lessons.json.

rockfall.description: The name of the scene prop (game/scene.json) whose blocks close the road and are removed when the pass opens.

edge.description: The scene site where the road meets the valley's edge.

snowBelowTemperature.description: Snow lies where the temperature at that height is below this.

treeLineBelowTemperature.description: No tree grows where the temperature at that height is below this.

margin.description: How far outside a region's edge, in blocks, the ground eases towards the edge's height.

treeClearance.description: The columns outside the edge that keep no trunk; below the margin.

floor.description: The least continentalness, in thousandths, at the region's edge.

shoreFloor.description: The least continentalness, in thousandths, at radius blocks out; a little inland of the sea. No higher than the floor.

radius.description: The distance in blocks over which the floor falls from floor to shoreFloor (and at that rate beyond it); at least the margin.

erosion.description: How the erosion round a region is shaped (B02b redo): calm out to fromRadius blocks from the edge, rugged from toRadius, back to the free world's by fadeRadius.

near.description: The least erosion, in thousandths, in the calm ring.

far.description: The most erosion, in thousandths, in the rugged belt; no higher than near.

fromRadius.description: Where the calm ring ends, in blocks from the edge.

toRadius.description: Where the rugged belt is full.

fadeRadius.description: Beyond this the free world's erosion is back.

headwater.description: How the rivers and lakes near a region give way to springs and ponds (B02b): none inside the margin, growing to the free world's over distance blocks beyond it.

distance.description: The blocks beyond the margin over which a river narrows and shallows to a stream that begins at a spring, and a lake shrinks to a pond.

blurRadius.description: The radius in columns of the blur the edge's height is smoothed with; 0 for none.

ease.description: The blocks over which the ground eases from the edge's own height to its blurred height; at most the margin.

exitCorridors.description: Roads that continue walkable beyond an exit of a region: from a point at the edge to a point outside.

cell.description: The first octave's size in blocks.

octaves.description: Each octave halves the cell and the weight.

warpCell.description: The warp field's cell in blocks.

warpBlocks.description: The farthest the warp bends the field, in blocks; 0 or absent for none.

round.description: For the ridged field: the thousandths over which the crest of each ridge is rounded; 0 or absent for a sharp crest.

chainBlocks.description: For the ridges field (B02b round 3): above 0, a chain: 1 on the noise's zero lines, falling in a straight slope to 0 at this many blocks from them, so every chain has the same width; 0 or absent for the squared ridge.

chainRound.description: The blocks over which the crest of a chain is rounded; at most chainBlocks.

spline.description: Control points [input, output] with rising inputs; an input is thousandths of the field's range.
